\chapter{Boolean Analysis — One Bit}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.OneBit
\section{Overview}

This module establishes hypercontractivity for functions on the single-bit cube
$\{\bbf\}^1$. It develops the Fourier description of one-bit functions, the core
real two-point inequality, and derives both the $(p,2)$- and $(2,q)$-hypercontractivity
theorems for one bit (together with the noise-operator duality and the supporting
power-mean, Cauchy--Schwarz, and H\"older-sharpness lemmas).

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Enumeration of the one-bit Boolean cube]
\lean{OneBit.boolCube1_univ}
\label{OneBit.boolCube1_univ}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube}
\difficulty{1}
On the one-dimensional Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^1$, whose points are the functions
from a single-element index set to $\{0,1\}$, the set of all points consists of exactly
the two constant functions: the one taking the value $0$ (false) and the one taking the
value $1$ (true).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The two subsets of a one-element set]
\lean{OneBit.finsetFin1_univ}
\label{OneBit.finsetFin1_univ}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Regarding $\mathrm{Fin}\,1 = \{0\}$ as a one-element set, its power set consists of
exactly two members: the empty set and the singleton $\{0\}$. That is, the collection of
all subsets of $\{0\}$ is $\{\emptyset,\ \{0\}\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The two constant one-bit inputs differ]
\lean{OneBit.boolCube1_ne}
\label{OneBit.boolCube1_ne}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Regarding the two Boolean-valued functions on the singleton index set $\mathrm{Fin}\,1 =
\{0\}$, the constant function taking the value $\mathit{false}$ everywhere and the
constant function taking the value $\mathit{true}$ everywhere are distinct.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empty subset differs from the singleton in $\mathrm{Fin}\,1$]
\lean{OneBit.finsetFin1_ne}
\label{OneBit.finsetFin1_ne}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Regarding the one-element index set $\mathrm{Fin}\,1 = \{0\}$, the empty subset
$\emptyset$ and the singleton subset $\{0\}$ are distinct as finite subsets of
$\mathrm{Fin}\,1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Value of a one-bit function at the false input]
\lean{OneBit.one_bit_val_false}
\label{OneBit.one_bit_val_false}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion, OneBit.finsetFin1_ne, OneBit.finsetFin1_univ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity $1$, and let $x_0\in\{0,1\}^1$
be the input whose single coordinate is $\mathit{false}$ (that is, the sign encoding of
that coordinate is $+1$). Then the value of $f$ at this input equals the sum of its
degree-zero and degree-one Fourier--Walsh coefficients:
\[
  f(x_0) \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset) + \hat f(\{0\}).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering a one-bit function's value from its Fourier coefficients]
\lean{OneBit.one_bit_val_true}
\label{OneBit.one_bit_val_true}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion, OneBit.finsetFin1_ne, OneBit.finsetFin1_univ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of a single bit, and write $\hat
f(\emptyset)$ and $\hat f(\{0\})$ for its two Fourier--Walsh coefficients, where $\{0\}$
is the singleton frequency consisting of the sole coordinate. Then the value of $f$ at
the input whose coordinate is set (the bit value corresponding to $-1$ under the sign
encoding) equals the difference of these two coefficients,
\[
  f(1) \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset) - \hat f(\{0\}).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Expected square of a noised one-bit function]
\lean{OneBit.expect_noiseOp_sq_one_bit}
\label{OneBit.expect_noiseOp_sq_one_bit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, OneBit.finsetFin1_ne, OneBit.finsetFin1_univ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity one, and let $\rho$ be any
real number. Then the expectation of the square of the noised function $T_\rho f$ under
the uniform measure is
\[
  \E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big] \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset)^2 \;+\; \rho^2\,\hat f(\{0\})^2,
\]
where $\emptyset$ and $\{0\}$ are the only two frequencies for a single coordinate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Expected $p$-th power of $|f|$ on one bit]
\lean{OneBit.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit}
\label{OneBit.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, OneBit.one_bit_val_false, OneBit.one_bit_val_true, OneBit.boolCube1_ne, OneBit.boolCube1_univ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of one bit and let $p\in\bbr$.
Writing $\hat f(\emptyset)$ and $\hat f(\{0\})$ for its two Fourier--Walsh coefficients,
the expectation of $|f|^p$ under the uniform measure is
\[
\E\big[\,|f|^p\,\big] \;=\; \frac{\big|\hat f(\emptyset) + \hat f(\{0\})\big|^p +
\big|\hat f(\emptyset) - \hat f(\{0\})\big|^p}{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of $L^r$ norms under the uniform measure]
\lean{OneBit.lp_norm_mono}
\label{OneBit.lp_norm_mono}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $r,s$ be real numbers with
$1\le r\le s$. Writing $\E$ for the expectation under the uniform probability measure on
$\{0,1\}^n$, the $L^r$ norm of $f$ is bounded by its $L^s$ norm:
\[
  \big(\E\big[\,|f|^{r}\,\big]\big)^{1/r}\;\le\;\big(\E\big[\,|f|^{s}\,\big]\big)^{1/s}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Two-point inequality on the unit interval]
\lean{OneBit.two_point_ineq_unit}
\label{OneBit.two_point_ineq_unit}
\leanok
\difficulty{7}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b003}
Let $p$ and $b$ be real numbers with $1 \le p \le 2$ and $0 \le b \le 1$. Then the
following inequality holds:
\[
  \big(1 + (p-1)b^2\big)^{p/2} \le \frac{(1+b)^p + (1-b)^p}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Two-point inequality in the case $a=0$]
\lean{OneBit.two_point_ineq_a_zero}
\label{OneBit.two_point_ineq_a_zero}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For every real number $p$ with $1 \le p \le 2$, one has $(p-1)^{p/2} \le 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A rearrangement inequality for a weighted square sum]
\lean{OneBit.noise_l2_abs_mono}
\label{OneBit.noise_l2_abs_mono}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $a, b, \rho$ be real numbers with $0 \le \rho \le 1$. Then
\[
a^2 + \rho^2 b^2 \;\le\; \left(\frac{|a+b| + |a-b|}{2}\right)^{\!2} + \rho^2
\left(\frac{|a+b| - |a-b|}{2}\right)^{\!2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The two-point inequality]
\lean{OneBit.two_point_ineq}
\label{OneBit.two_point_ineq}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b002,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b003
}
\uses{OneBit.two_point_ineq_unit}
\difficulty{6}
Let $a, b \in \bbr$, let $1 \le p \le 2$, and let $\rho \ge 0$ satisfy $\rho^2 \le p -
1$. Then
\[
  \big(a^2 + \rho^2 b^2\big)^{1/2} \le \left(\frac{|a+b|^p + |a-b|^p}{2}\right)^{1/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-bit $(p,2)$-hypercontractivity]
\lean{OneBit.one_bit_p2_hypercontractivity}
\label{OneBit.one_bit_p2_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b002,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b003
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, OneBit.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit, OneBit.expect_noiseOp_sq_one_bit, OneBit.two_point_ineq}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function on a single bit, and let $p$ be a
real number with $1\le p\le 2$. Suppose $\rho\ge 0$ satisfies $\rho^2\le p-1$. Writing
$T_\rho$ for the noise operator and $\E$ for expectation under the uniform measure on
$\{0,1\}^1$,
\[
  \big(\E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big]\big)^{1/2}\;\le\;\big(\E\big[|f|^p\big]\big)^{1/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Signum times argument equals absolute value]
\lean{OneBit.sign_mul_self}
\label{OneBit.sign_mul_self}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $x$, the product of its sign and itself equals its absolute value:
$\operatorname{sign}(x)\cdot x = \abs{x}$, where $\operatorname{sign}(x)$ is $1$ if
$x>0$, $-1$ if $x<0$, and $0$ if $x=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute value of the sign of a nonzero real]
\lean{OneBit.abs_sign_eq_one}
\label{OneBit.abs_sign_eq_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every nonzero real number $x$, the sign function $\operatorname{sign}(x)$, equal to
$+1$ when $x > 0$ and $-1$ when $x < 0$, satisfies $\abs{\operatorname{sign}(x)} = 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the expectation of a nonnegative function]
\lean{OneBit.expect_nonneg_of_nonneg}
\label{OneBit.expect_nonneg_of_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function that is nonnegative at every point,
so $f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in \{0,1\}^n$. Then its expectation under the uniform
measure is nonnegative: $\E[f] \ge 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Expectation of a constant function]
\lean{OneBit.expect_const_eq}
\label{OneBit.expect_const_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{1}
For any real number $c$, the constant Boolean function $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ with
$f(x)=c$ for all $x$ has expectation $\E[f]=c$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cauchy–Schwarz for the Boolean inner product]
\lean{OneBit.cauchy_schwarz_bool}
\label{OneBit.cauchy_schwarz_bool}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be Boolean functions, and write $\E[h] = 2^{-n}\sum_{x
\in \{0,1\}^n} h(x)$ for the expectation under the uniform measure and $\langle f,
g\rangle = \E[f\cdot g]$ for the $L^2$ inner product. Then
\[
  \langle f, g\rangle \;\le\; \big(\E[f^2]\big)^{1/2}\,\big(\E[g^2]\big)^{1/2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Sharpness of Hölder's inequality on the hypercube]
\lean{OneBit.holder_sharpness}
\label{OneBit.holder_sharpness}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, OneBit.expect_nonneg_of_nonneg, OneBit.expect_const_eq}
\difficulty{6}
Fix a dimension $n$ and Hölder conjugate exponents $p, q$ (so $p, q > 1$ and $\tfrac1p +
\tfrac1q = 1$). For a function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ write $\norm{g}_r =
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,|g|^r\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/r}$ for its $L^r$ norm under the uniform measure
on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then for every function $u : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ there exists a function
$f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ with $\norm{f}_p \le 1$ and $\norm{u}_q \le \langle f,
u\rangle$, where $\langle f, u\rangle = \E[f\cdot u]$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{Bonami.expect_sq_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_self_adjoint, OneBit.cauchy_schwarz_bool, OneBit.holder_sharpness}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p$ and $p'$ be Hölder conjugate exponents, so that $1/p + 1/p' = 1$, and suppose $1
\le p$. Write $T_{\sqrt{p-1}}$ for the noise operator with rate $\rho = \sqrt{p-1}$
acting on Boolean functions of a single bit. Suppose that
\[
\E\!\left[\,\bigl|T_{\sqrt{p-1}} f\bigr|^{2}\,\right]^{1/2} \;\le\;
\E\!\left[\,|f|^{p}\,\right]^{1/p}
\]
holds for every one-bit Boolean function $f$. Then for every one-bit Boolean function
$g$,
\[
\E\!\left[\,\bigl|T_{\sqrt{p-1}} g\bigr|^{p'}\,\right]^{1/p'} \;\le\;
\E\!\left[\,|g|^{2}\,\right]^{1/2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, OneBit.noise_operator_duality, OneBit.one_bit_p2_hypercontractivity}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a real exponent $q \ge 2$, and let $g : \{0,1\} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of
arity one. Write $\norm{h}_p = \left(\E\,|h|^{p}\right)^{1/p}$ for the $L^p$ norm taken
with respect to the uniform measure, and let $T_\rho$ denote the noise operator. Then,
with noise parameter $\rho = 1/\sqrt{q-1}$,
\[
  \norm{T_{1/\sqrt{q-1}}\, g}_q \;\le\; \norm{g}_2 .
\]
\end{theorem}
